market.category: Caffeine trackers and sleep planning tools
market.audience: Coffee, tea, pre-workout, and energy drink users who want to understand timing before another dose
market.problem: A basic caffeine log records the decision after it happens and leaves the user to translate intake into a bedtime impact
market.advantage: Caffeine Tracker previews a proposed dose and time against a personal bedtime forecast before anything is logged
market.competitive_context: The category commonly offers drink logs and caffeine decay charts. This app centers the pre-log decision, dose-specific timing, and visible uncertainty range

proof_points.claim: The Now screen shows current and bedtime estimates with a visible half-life range
The drink preview compares the current bedtime forecast with a proposed dose before logging
The Timeline shows caffeine intake and modeled bedtime values over time
The Body tab compares recorded sleep and cardiovascular data on higher-caffeine days against lower ones, all read from Apple Health

story.throughline: Understand tonight, preview the next dose, then see how the estimate lines up with this body's own recorded nights

frames.header: Know what may remain at bedtime

pitch.benefit: See a bedtime estimate without translating a day of drinks by hand
pitch.problem: An intake total alone does not answer what may remain tonight
pitch.advantage: The Now screen keeps current and bedtime estimates together with a visible uncertainty range
pitch.proof: The literal Now screen shows estimated caffeine now, at bedtime, and a 4 to 6 hour range

frames.header: Preview a drink before you log it

pitch.benefit: Compare a proposed drink against the bedtime forecast before saving it
pitch.problem: Most caffeine logs reveal the impact only after the entry exists
pitch.advantage: Every quick-log drink opens a preview, so dose and timing come before the log action
pitch.proof: The literal preview sheet compares the current and proposed bedtime estimates and the latest modeled time for that dose

frames.header: See caffeine next to your sleep

pitch.benefit: See what Apple Health recorded on higher-caffeine days next to lower ones
pitch.problem: A caffeine number means little without this body's own recorded nights
pitch.advantage: The Body tab compares recorded sleep, resting heart rate and HRV against intake, and withholds a result when the sample is too small
pitch.proof: The literal Body tab shows recorded sleep and cardiovascular comparisons read from Apple Health, described as observations rather than effects

pitch.benefit: Compare intake and bedtime estimates across days
pitch.problem: One day cannot show whether timing habits are changing
pitch.advantage: The timeline pairs daily intake with modeled bedtime values
pitch.proof: The literal Timeline shows daily intake bars with average daily and average at-bedtime values

frames.header: See the drinks behind the total

pitch.benefit: Trace the running estimate back to the individual drinks behind it
pitch.problem: A first launch can show a number the user never entered, because Apple Health already held caffeine from another app
pitch.advantage: The Now card breaks its estimate into per-dose shares, so no figure appears without its source
pitch.proof: The literal breakdown sheet lists each logged dose and its share of the current estimate

frames.header: Tune the half-life to your body

pitch.benefit: Set the half-life the forecast uses instead of accepting one default
pitch.problem: A fixed five-hour half-life does not fit every person
pitch.advantage: The half-life is adjustable and the forecast still shows a four to six hour reference range around it
pitch.proof: The literal Settings screen shows the half-life control and the bedtime preference the forecast uses
